title: fix(app-shell): Studio's nav save leaves out entries with no target, and its banner clears on the next landed save (objectui#11776)
body:
Fixes #11776
Clause-②: no

Studio's navigation editor no longer sends an unbound "Add nav item" entry, so autosave stops failing while one is on the canvas. The error banner from a failed nav save now clears when a later nav save lands. Each row's remove control can now be reached and used from the keyboard.

Left out of this PR: the Changes panel's no-op "Update" row (the card's fourth expectation). The seat cut it to objectui#11807, and nothing here touches the Changes panel.

## What changed

- **What a nav save sends.** `navPayloadOf` (in `AppNavCanvas.tsx`) returns the editor's navigation with every entry that names no target for its `type` left out, at every depth.
  - A `group` is always kept. An entry with no `type` is still left out, as before.
  - The target of each `type` is read from one table, `NAV_TARGET_READS`. The card's own `navTarget` reads the same table, so what a card shows as its target and what the save treats as a target cannot drift apart.
  - `doNavSave` calls it. The spec and the server are unchanged.
- **The placeholder stays on the canvas, in its place.** While the buffer holds an entry the save left out, the buffer stays dirty.
  - Without this, the re-read that a landed save triggers would install the served draft over the placeholder, and it would vanish right after the autosave. This was measured by mutation M1 below.
  - Binding the entry is the edit that sends it.
- **The banner.** The nav save's failure now lives in its own state, `navError`, shown in the same canvas banner.
  - It clears when a nav save lands, on a conflict "reload", and when a read-only answer puts the nav buffer back.
  - A failure the open leaf is showing (the pillar's `error`) is left alone. A pin covers this.
- **The remove control** is always mounted and in the tab order. It is shown on card hover, on the card's keyboard focus, and on its own keyboard focus.
  - While hidden it has no width and gives back the row's gap, so the card lays out exactly as on BASE.

## The PM's hypotheses, measured

- **H1, confirmed.** "Add nav item" inserts `{ id, type: 'object' }`, and the old filter in `doNavSave` dropped only entries with no `type`.
  - Chromium payloads are in the browser section below.
  - Nesting: the canvas adds entries only at the root, and the inspector binds only root entries. So an unbound nested entry cannot be produced through Studio's UI, and served drafts are spec-valid. The recursion is pinned at the function level (a placeholder inside a `group`, and inside an `object`'s nested views).
- **H2, confirmed.** The producer is `InterfacesPillar`'s pillar-local `error` state, set by `doNavSave`'s catch.
  - The only place the pillar ever cleared it was the start of the leaf-draft load effect.
  - The shared `useDraftAutoSave` holds no error state and is untouched, so no other pillar is involved.
- **H3, partly wrong.** The control was already a `span` with `role="button"`, `tabIndex={0}`, and an accessible name ("Remove nav item"). So no `engine.*` row is added.
  - It was not hidden with opacity. It was mounted only while a JS `hover` state was true (`onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave`), so for a keyboard user it was not in the DOM at all.
- **H4, confirmed, with one correction.** The id backfill for a root entry with no `id` ran after the filter and used the filtered index, so leaving an entry out moved a generated id. A spec-valid `separator` may have no id, so this was reachable.
  - The backfill now uses the editor position, before anything is left out.
  - What is sent is the editor's array minus the untargeted entries, in order, with the same object references (pinned).

## Real-browser reading (dev-only harness, not committed)

Chromium, 1440×900. The harness mounted `InterfacesPillar` the way the surface mounts it, over the real console metadata client. A Playwright route handler played the server: it parsed every app PUT with the spec's `AppSchema` and answered refusals in the `/meta` write door's issue shape. The harness was then removed (`git status` clean).

| Step | BASE `8273f4b` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Add nav item, leave it unbound, autosave | PUT **400**, navigation `nav_home, nav_landing, nav_item_3` (type object, no objectName). Banner: "• navigation.2.objectName — Invalid input: expected string, received undefined" | PUT **200**, navigation `nav_home, nav_landing`. No banner. `nav_item_3` still on the canvas, third. Leave guard holds |
| Remove the placeholder, autosave | PUT 200, but **the banner stays** | PUT 200, no banner |
| Add two entries, bind the second, then the first | (n/a) | PUT 200 `…, nav_item_4`, then PUT 200 `…, nav_item_3, nav_item_4`. Leave guard released |
| A failed nav save (503), then remove that row with Tab + Enter | (n/a) | Banner "Service unavailable", then PUT 200 and **the banner clears** |
| Remove control at rest / card hovered / card keyboard-focused / itself focused | at rest: not in the DOM | opacity 0, width 0 / 1, 24px / 1, 24px / 1, 24px with `:focus-visible`. Tab from the card lands on it |
| Card label widths at rest (px) | 102, 85, 128 | 102, 85, 128 |
| Done after everything is bound | (n/a) | closes editing |

The label-width row matters. The first version of this branch always reserved the control's 24px, which cost every label 32px at rest ("Landing menu" truncated at 53 of 79px). Commit `194fa98` fixes that.

## Pins

- `AppNavCanvas.navPayload-11776.test.tsx`:
  - A parity pin walks every member of the spec's `NavigationItemSchema` discriminator, read from the schema itself. It holds that the save leaves an entry out exactly when the spec refuses the bare entry, and keeps it once its target is set.
  - Further pins: `doc` (by `doc` or `book`), `action` (by `actionDef.actionName`), no-`type`, the empty-string boundary (the spec accepts any string), an undeclared `type` (sent, for the server to refuse by name), nesting at every depth, order and references, and the all-bound control.
  - Keyboard pins: the control is in every row without a pointer, has an accessible name, is reached by Tab after its card, carries the visibility classes, and Enter or Space removes that entry only.
- `StudioDesignSurface.navPlaceholderSave-11776.test.tsx`: the pillar with an `AppSchema`-parsing server double. Pins:
  - left unbound: not sent, and the spec takes the save;
  - the entry stays on the canvas, in its place, through the re-read;
  - binding later sends it in its place;
  - control: an all-bound nav is sent exactly as the editor holds it;
  - a failed then landed save clears the banner;
  - control: a landed nav save leaves the open leaf's failure in place.
- **Fixture triage.** The objectui#11189, #11204, #11232 and #11167 suites used a bare "Add nav item" as their edit. Their doubles parse nothing, so they accepted an entry the server refuses.
  - Each edit is now Add plus binding to a fixture object in the inspector.
  - Two "sends nothing" pins in the #11232 suite would have passed without testing anything once a bare Add stopped being sent. They again test an edit that would be sent.
  - What each pin checks is unchanged.

## Reverse check and ablations

- **BASE source with the new pins** (`git checkout 8273f4b` of the two source files, restored from `HEAD`, blob hashes equal, `git diff HEAD` empty): 38 failed, 5 passed.
  - The 5 that pass: the two spec-only pins, the fixture pin, and the two controls.
  - Direction as predicted. The first pillar pin received `accepted: false` with `{ id: 'nav_item_3', type: 'object' }` in the payload.
- **M1** (via `ablation-replace.mjs`; anchor 1 → 0, blob moved, restored to `HEAD`): `if (sent.unmoved() && !leftOut)` → `if (sent.unmoved())`. The "stays on the canvas" pin fails: the rail shows only `Home menu, Landing menu` after the re-read.
- **M2**: the landed-save `setNavError(null)` removed. The banner pin fails: "Service unavailable" is still shown.
  - The first M2 attempt was refused by the tool, because its replacement was a substring of its anchor. That attempt was a no-op and is not counted. The re-run landed.

## Gates, on `2e408c7`

- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`: exit 0. It ran before the edits; the dependency closure is upstream of every touched file.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on 60 files: every `StudioDesignSurface*`, `AppNavCanvas*` and `AppPreview*` test, `studio-locale.i18n`, `ResourceEditPage.navDeepLink-11153`, and `navSurface.test.ts`. Result: `Test Files 60 passed (60)`, `Tests 420 passed (420)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0, and the script name was echoed. `--listFilesOnly` shows all six touched test files are in the `tsconfig.test.json` program.
- Exit 0 for each:
  - `check:control-bytes`
  - `check:new-line-citations` (0 new)
  - `check:changeset-claims`
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`
  - `check:vi-mock-inherit`
  - `check:vi-mock-override-shape`
  - `check:test-path-roots`
  - `check:metadata-write-doors`
  - `check-changeset-presence` (1 changeset declared)
  - `check-changeset-no-major`
- **ESLint on the 8 touched files only.** CI's `pnpm lint` (turbo `eslint .` per package) owns the full run. The narrowed run gave 0 errors, and its 16 warnings are exactly BASE's 16 for the two sources, by rule. The narrowing is proven by three facts:
  - the population is CI's own `eslint .` under the root `eslint.config.js`;
  - the count of 8 files comes from `--format json`;
  - the config enables no type-aware linting (no `projectService`, `parserOptions.project` or type-checked preset), so this diff cannot change a verdict in an untouched file.

## Deviations and fence

- `navPayloadOf` is a module export of `AppNavCanvas.tsx`, as the PM's route allowed. It does not reach the package entry: `index.ts` re-exports a named list, and `exports` has only `.`. The `react-refresh/only-export-components` disable follows the precedent of `renderStudioGridList`.
- No `@object-ui/types` member, prop, or `packages/i18n/**` key is added. Every file is inside the claim's surface.

## Acceptance notes (not carded; carrier: none)

- **"Done" with an unbound entry on the canvas keeps nav editing open, and nothing says why.** This follows objectui#11189's rule that "Done" never closes over an unsent edit. The entry is selected when it is added, so its inspector shows "Choose an object; the menu item will open its record list." This is left for the seat to rule on.
- **A browser reload drops an unbound entry.** It is never stored, because the spec refuses it and keeping it would need a draft-schema change. The leave guard warns before the reload.
- **The leaf's own draft save (`doSave`) never clears its own failure on a later landed save either.** It is the same class of defect, read in source only, and outside this claim's surface.
- **The metadata-admin app editor (`AppPreview`, off-limits here) uses the same canvas "Add nav item".** Whether its save sends the placeholder was not measured.
- **The remove control is a `role="button"` span inside the card's button element.** Chromium focuses it and activates it (measured). Other browser engines were not measured.
- **After Enter removes the focused row, focus falls to the document body.**

Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 1 PM; implemented in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01DrKzdPdyLLBW3qpZ4vtk7z`.
